chunk_map.heading: 1. Treat CI as feedback into the loop, not a gate to pass
2. Fan out review; converge on the pattern
3. Tier by blast radius. Make the Tier-1 case on your own PRs
Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice
4. Eval latency is part of the loop
Cherny pairs a fast check with a slow one
5. Skills don't just live in your kit. Promote them into the CI surface
The skill catalogue scales: plan time to company-wide
6. Get out fast. Learn from real customers safely
Agents need the outer loop's signal too
Where this fits in your AE101 arc

chunk_map_note: Prior instance's chunk_map (9 entries) merged each move's sub-heading ('Two proofs the loop compounds', 'Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice', 'Cherny pairs a fast check with a slow one', 'The skill catalogue scales', 'Agents need the outer loop's signal too') into its parent numbered move. The renderer cuts at every `##` — signals.slide_count=13 confirms 13 body headings, not 6. Re-chunked correctly here; this changes which chunk several bolded handles land in for rule 9.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate, chunk 5 "Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice" line 37: "**Stripe** is a different point on the same spectrum." 'the same spectrum' was never literally named as 'spectrum' in the prior chunk (4, Intercom tiering), but stays inside: chunk 4 established the trade-off (gate strictness vs cycle time, sorted by risk) as its whole subject, and chunk 5 opens by contrasting Stripe's bet against it — immediate continuation of the previous slide's subject, the carved-out case. Also checked line 63 "Larson at Imprint consults the same shape of artifact at plan time" — 'artifact' resolves against AGENTS.md/rules-files/pre-commit-hooks named in the immediately preceding chunk (8). No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found across the 14 chunks.

Closest candidate, chunk 12 line 85: "The loop at your desk is the one this training closed... This piece is the same loop, run by engineers who've been at it longer." Names the referent by content ('the loop', 'this training') not by file position ('the opening lecture said'), and functions as the closer summing the whole file against the training arc — the explicitly carved-out case, not a violation. No 'the opening lecture said X' style positional callback anywhere in the file; the only cross-doc gesture is the module-flag conditional lede (line 5), which names M6 by content ('two sessions of the same task, gap diagnosis...'), not position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 line 5 (module-flag branch): "Two sessions of the same task, gap diagnosis, a second skill in `~/.claude/skills/`, one rule cut from `./CLAUDE.local.md`." Checked against `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` (M6, the flagged module): 'Start here' (line 25) opens on 'two sessions of the same task' (M4 send-off + M5 re-send); 'What You'll Learn' line 14 has student Diagnose gaps routing to 'memory, sharper verifier, or new skill'; line 15 has student Cut one rule from `./CLAUDE.local.md`. All three named beats exist in the current M6 file. 'a second skill in ~/.claude/skills/' is a plausible compression of M6's skill-authoring LOs (lines 14, 19, 60) rather than a literal quote of that path in the module — module speaks of the skill destination generically, not the dotfile path — but the beat (gap routes to a new skill) is real, so this clears rule 3's 'beat exists' test; a literal-path mismatch, if one existed, would be a technical-class concern, not a slides one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: No guess-before-reveal live-demo structure anywhere in the file; the six 'Try this Monday' prompts are self-directed take-home actions, not a narrated demo with a guess line followed by an outcome line.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate, chunk 1 (shortest chunk, lines 7-10): header + one full paragraph (line 9, three sentences) + a Monday action (line 17, actually in chunk 2 under the corrected chunking — chunk 1 itself still carries a complete self-standing claim on line 9: 'A failing CI run is signal... Each red build sharpens the next session.'). Not a wait-state or single context-dependent bullet — a self-carrying claim. Every other chunk (checked all 14) carries at least one full paragraph plus a named practitioner example.

Closest candidate, chunk 4 header (line 29) "3. Tier by blast radius. Make the Tier-1 case on your own PRs" — chunk 4's actual content (lines 29-34) only covers the tiering definition and Intercom's numbers; the 'make the case on your own PRs' action doesn't land until chunk 5's Try-this-Monday (line 41), under a different header ('Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice'). This is a promise fulfilled one chunk later rather than in the labelled chunk, but nothing in chunk 4 asserts something the content contradicts — rule 6's test is contradiction, not full-coverage — so it stays inside. Checked all 14 headers against their own chunk content; no header is contradicted by what follows it.

Checked all five sub-items. (1) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' banned construction: only one 'Not' sentence in the file, line 31 'Not all PRs deserve the same gate.' — a single negation, not the triple. (2) Anaphora triple: line 9 'About which memory rule should have caught the mistake upstream. About which verifier was too soft. About which skill ran on auto-pilot when it should have paused.' — three parallel legs, but each names a genuinely distinct concrete diagnostic target (rule / verifier / skill), clearing the 'third leg carries NEW concrete content' bar rather than tripping the intensifying-repetition ban. (3) Self-grading superlatives: grepped 'one of the most', 'most useful', 'most powerful', 'game-chang', 'revolutioniz' — zero hits; 'The best' is used as a repeated topic-sentence device (= 'the best engineers') describing external practitioners, never grading this training's own content. (4) Number + retraction: checked every stat (52%→80%, 19.2%/14.6min/75.8min/86%, 1,000+/week, 131,246/48,095/5,169/3m39s/0.6%) — none paired with a hedge/retraction. (5) Abstraction-noun stacks: closest candidate line 63 'the same shape of artifact' — resolves concretely via the immediately preceding chunk (AGENTS.md, rules files, pre-commit hooks) rather than floating free; not swapped for a fully concrete phrase but not opaque either. (6) Empty-leg verb triplets: none found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped the banned-term list (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood) against the body: zero hits for compendium/firing/forcing function/beat/mood. 'surface' appears twice as ordinary engineering usage — line 31 'different review surfaces' (analogous to 'attack surface', not our authoring-vocabulary noun sense) and 'CI surface' (chunk 8 header, same ordinary sense). 'gap diagnosis', 'packaging', 'the loop' are this training's own arc-earned spine vocabulary (M4-M6), not repo/maintainer dialect — out of scope for §8, in scope for §1's arc-earned carve-out instead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Budget is ≤1 bolded element per slide (no menu/lookup-surface exemption applies — this is narrative essay prose, not a scanned reading list). Six of the fourteen chunks carry 2-3 bolded handles each: chunk 2 "Two proofs the loop compounds" (lines 11-18) has THREE — line 13 '**Klaassen at Every**', line 15 '**Cursor's Bugbot**', line 17 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 3 "2. Fan out review..." has two — line 23 '**Cloudflare engineering**', line 27 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 5 "Stripe bets on the sandbox..." has two — line 37 '**Stripe**', line 41 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 7 "Cherny pairs a fast check..." has two — line 51 '**Cherny on Claude Code**', line 53 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 9 "The skill catalogue scales..." has THREE — line 63 '**Larson at Imprint**', line 65 '**Charles runs Ramp's Dojo**', line 67 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 11 "Agents need the outer loop's signal too" has THREE — line 77 '**Majors at Honeycomb**', line 79 '**Wolff on the Claude Code team**', line 81 '**Try this Monday.**'. The pattern is consistent: a practitioner-name bold plus a 'Try this Monday.' bold, sometimes plus a second practitioner. Prior instance flagged this rule but against the WRONG (merged) chunk map, citing chunks 1-6; corrected chunk indices are 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 above. Chunks 4, 6, 8 correctly carry exactly one bold each (within budget).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Pick one bolded handle per chunk — likely the recurring 'Try this Monday.' action-cue as the checklist-item handle — and drop practitioner-name bolding to plain text; where two practitioners share a chunk (9, 11), only one chunk's worth of budget is available, so consider whether the sub-heading split should carry its own '##' to give each practitioner their own slide instead.
